findings.F1: On wide days (range at least 1.5 times the 20-day swing), the next-day excess return falls steadily as the close moves up the range. Closes in the low third rise +0.84 % (t 2.56 with cases of one day together, 354 days), the middle third +0.25 % (t 0.67) and the high third −0.35 % (t −1.33). The low-close rebound is the only part that stands out, and the map already holds it as long agitated rebound books (039-02, 044-01, 045-01) plus the many long books that act in every profile.
findings.F2: In a falling 60-day trend on wide days, high closes are followed by −1.02 % the next day (t −1.87, 95 days) and low closes by +0.94 % (t 1.55, 134 days). This points the tested idea's way in folds B and C but does not reach t 2. Within closes above mid-range in falling or choppy coins, the correlation of close location with the next-day excess move is −0.02 over 499 cases, so the "nearer the high, larger the fall" grading is not there.
findings.F3: The book's active bars split by close location. The top third fell −1.93 % (t −2.45, 68 cases), while the lower two thirds rose +2.49 % (t 2.64) and +2.78 % (t 2.33). The standardised close-location forecast shorted mid and lower closes that rebounded, which is where the book lost.
findings.F4: Falling-trend high closes on wide days are not steady across windows or years. They fell in 2018, 2019 and 2020 (−1.14 %, −1.24 %, −2.71 %) but rose +0.65 % in 2021. Across windows, w17 shows +1.06 % and w11 +0.50 %, against w13 −2.04 % and w16 −1.77 %, none with t beyond 2.4.
findings.F5: Weekday patterns vanish once cases of one day are taken together. Wednesday is −0.50 % (t −1.29) and Thursday and Friday are +0.41 % and +0.38 % (t 1.34 and 1.52), against unclustered t near 2.8. By volatility tercile, the next-day excess move is flat (t −1.10 to 0.75).
findings.F6: In a rising trend, wide days with high closes continue up the next day by +0.80 % (t 1.76, 179 days). This repeats the rising range-top continuation books the map already holds (033-03.b2, 034-01.b1).

no_ideas: The only pattern that stands out once same-day cases are counted together is the wide-day low-close rebound (F1), which the portfolio already holds; the tested high-close fade, its grading, and the weekday, volatility and rising-trend angles stay under t 2 or repeat held books (F2–F6).
